analysis.title: Quantitative Conviction: Bullish PLTR & CVS; Cautious WEIR, WAT, SARO
key_insights: UBS Sales desk note (Amandine-Parisa Kara, 30-Oct-2026) overlays quantitative signals on stocks where UBS Research and Sales have the highest conviction ahead of earnings, to test where quant indicators support the fundamental view and where they diverge.

Headline calls: bullish PLTR and CVS, cautious WEIR, WAT and SARO. The extracted text does not include the per-name signal readings, which sit in the highlighted screen images and the attached slide deck.
US names reporting w/c 2 November: AAPL, PLTR, AMD, APTV, ETN, BROS, MCD, SITM, ZBH, CMI, DVN, GH, MTD, SARO, TECH, NTRA, WAT, CVS.
European names reporting w/c 2 November: CON GR, HEI GR, WEIR LN, ENX FP.
Screens combine signals from UBS Quant Research (HF X EN, ML EPS, HF X Retail) and UBS Systematic Advisory.

HF X EN identifies stocks likely to show pre-earnings announcement drift, using Earnings Surprise Nowcasts, crowding and analyst survey data. The strongest signal combinations generate up to +4.3% excess return in the 60 trading days before earnings.

ML EPS ranks stocks by machine-learning forecasts of EPS growth. Long the top third and short the bottom third returned 5.6% annualized with a Sharpe ratio of 0.55, versus 1.5% annualized and 0.16 Sharpe for consensus-based forecasts.
Hedge fund crowding has returned 5.3% annualized with a Sharpe of 0.83 globally since 2017. Crowding momentum (12-month change in positioning) returned 6.9% annualized with a Sharpe of 0.60.
HF X SI double-sorts on days-to-cover: lightly shorted, highly crowded longs and heavily shorted, short-crowded shorts. UBS says this beats either signal alone on a risk-adjusted basis.

HF X Retail goes long stocks where hedge fund crowding momentum is rising while retail investors are net sellers, and the reverse on the short side. It returned 12.2% annualized with a Sharpe of 1.07, versus 0.60 for crowding momentum alone.
HF X LO targets crowded hedge fund longs that mutual funds underweight. It returned +8.3% annualized in the US (information ratio 1.18) and +5.0% in Europe (information ratio 0.88).
